summary: Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Presidency College Chennai, Presidency University, and University of Calcutta. He directed the Bhutia Boarding School in 1874 and translated Tibetan for Bengal's government (1881–1904).

Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Manipur University, studying under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).
Saroja Bhate (born 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from circa 1988 to 2002.
Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian. He studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College Chennai, University of Madras, and Balliol College, Oxford, and later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (circa 1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Voorhees College, Madras Christian College, and University of Madras. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu universities, professor at Oxford and Calcutta, and Chancellor of Delhi University.

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Pali Department at the University of Calcutta, attested in 2011.

Satiranjan Sen was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University. He served as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948), he worked at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1963) and the University of Rajasthan (~1963–1970).

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Krishnagar Government College and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das, he was Principal of Sanskrit College and University and Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (circa 1942–1956) and became Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya, Ramachandra Jha (attested 1970), and Ramachandra Sastri (attested 1970).

Satoru Harada (born 1947) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar with an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and as professor at Kokushikan University (2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Esho Mikogami (attested 1996). He has held lecturer and part-time lecturer positions at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1995) and Ryukoku University (2003, 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and later served as a lecturer there, attested from 2015 to 2017.

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Bukkyo University and University of Michigan, he taught at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he became professor (1996) and president (2014).
Satoshi Kawano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki specializes in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University and served there as an assistant professor (attested 2016–2020).
